question.leadin: Answer some questions about mink in history.
question.text: This president claimed that his wife, Pat, "doesn't have a mink coat" in his "Checkers" speech. This man was later forced to resign over the Watergate scandal, despite declaring "I am not a crook".
question.clue: A ruling in which this man was the respondent cited Accardi v. Shaughnessy to assert the power of the Attorney General and notes that "in camera inspection" is not a substantial diminishment of communications.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the presidency of John F. Kennedy.
swap.text: The Kennedy administration approved this failed 1961 invasion of Cuba led by Cuban exiles, which increased tensions, leading to the Cuban Missile Crisis.
swap.clue: This event's failure led Allen Dulles to be forced to resign.

question.leadin: Harry Truman visited this city nearly a dozen times as President, establishing a "Little White House."
question.text: Name this southernmost city of the continental United States. The 2,300-plus miles of U.S. Route 1 run from Fort Kent in Maine south through Miami to this city.
question.clue: This island was a frequent destination for Harry S. Truman, leading a neighborhood here to be named Truman Annex.

swap.text: One of the largest riots in United States history occurred in New York in 1863 when this system was instituted, and it also was a motivation behind many student riots during the Vietnam War before this system was discontinued in 1973.
swap.clue: General John Wool put down one demonstration against this practice, in which Irish laborers killed at least a dozen black men in a New York riot during the Civil War.

question.text: Francisco Duran shot at who he believed to be this President. He claimed that he was trying to destroy an alien "mist" surrounding the White House that controlled the U.S. Government.
question.clue: Policies implemented during this man's presidency included "Don't Ask, Don't Tell", and NAFTA.

swap.leadin: The brothers Alfred and William oversaw their design and construction.
swap.text: Give the name of these planned suburban communities, many of which were built in the 1940's and 50's. The homogeneity of these communities were symbolic of post-World War II mass-produced suburbs.
swap.clue: Thurgood Marshall fought against the discriminative policies of these places, like the 25th clause of a standard lease that allowed only Caucasians to become residents of these places.

question.leadin: This president's National Commission on Excellence in Education criticized the country's schools in the report A Nation at Risk.
question.text: Name this president whose other children-related policies included the anti-drug "Just Say No" campaign, which was devised by his wife.
question.clue: This man described a group of people as having "Slipped the surly bonds of Earth to touch the face of God" in one speech and endorsed Barry Goldwater in his "A Time For Choosing" speech.

swap.leadin: Identify some candidates from the 1964 U.S. Presidential election.
swap.text: Nicknamed "Mr. Conservative," this Republican from Texas became the primary opponent of LBJ, but that's not saying much as he lost a very lopsided election.
swap.clue: Ronald Reagan gave his "A Time for Choosing" speech in support of this politician.

question.leadin: Identify these British folks who rebelled against Catholic Church doctrine.
question.text: This group, started by Gerrard Winstanley in 1649, was an offshoot of the Levelers and argued for radical Christian communitarianism and the cultivation of neglected land.
question.clue: Led early on by William Everard, the philosophy of this group was put forth in The New Law of Righteousness, the primary text by its major leader Gerrard Winstanley.

swap.leadin: The economist Nathaniel Baum-Snow found that this program led to a 17% reduction in the population of major American cities between 1950 and 1990.
swap.text: Name this massive federal project built partly for defense purposes. The Overtown neighborhood of Miami lost much of its population due to this project.
swap.answerHtml: Interstate Highway System [prompt on highway; accept but DO NOT REVEAL Dwight D. Eisenhower National System of Interstate and Defense Highways]
swap.clue: As First Lady, Lady Bird Johnson advocated for the passage of a "Beautification Act" to improve this system.

question.text: The original Watergate break-in was organized by covert White House agents given this colloquial nickname. This name was given to this group because its original goal was to plug information leaks.
question.clue: Members of this group went on to join the Committee to Re-elect the President.

swap.text: After the death of Kennedy, Oswald apparently killed this Dallas police officer 45 minutes later. Conspiracy theorists claim this man's murder was part of the overall scheme to kill both JFK and Oswald.

question.text: This naval officer stated he had the best seat in the house to watch the Gulf of Tonkin affair. As a VP candidate, he opened a debate with the questions "Who am I? Why am I here?"
question.clue: In 1992, this running mate of Ross Perot opened a debate by asking "Who am I? Why am I here?" This vice admiral commanded the USS Ticonderoga during the Gulf of Tonkin incident.

swap.text: Millard Tydings headed a committee investigating this man's claims. This man inspired a political cartoon by Herblock showing an elephant backing away from a shaky stack of paint cans.
swap.clue: This man succeeded Robert La Follette, Jr. in his highest ranking position, and he also chaired the Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations.

question.text: To confirm the reliability of adding submarine-based missiles to U.S. nuclear defenses, this first nuclear-powered submarine was sent on a trip through the North Pole in 1958.

swap.leadin: It originally referred to dead men, but its best known usage originated in 1831 to refer to an important voting bloc.
swap.text: Give this term, whose best known use refers to the large number of Americans who did not demonstrate against the Vietnam War or participate in national discourse and stems from a 1969 election speech
swap.clue: Republicans sometimes use it to explain election outcomes in which the media predicted that the Democratic candidate would win easily, but on election day, the Republican candidate came out on top.

question.leadin: Identify the following about some participants in the Watergate scandal who later wrote books about it.
question.text: Jeb Stuart Magruder, the author of An American Life: One Man's Road to Watergate served as the deputy director of this organization. It had the appropriate acronym of "CREEP".
question.answer: The Committee to Reelect the President
question.clue: This organization caused the Watergate break-in to become a full-fledged scandal after they paid for the burglars' legal fees. This organization was created to help a certain man win the election of 1972.

swap.text: Children and escapees from Cuba to Miami were processed at this "Ellis Island of the South". Today, it is a contemporary art museum associated with Miami Dade College.

question.text: Under the leadership of saleswoman Brownie Wise, this line of products was widely sold in the 1950s through a form of direct marketing called the "party plan," which involved women hosting social events for their friends and neighbors to try this line of products.

swap.leadin: Howard Zinn actively encouraged jury nullification while testifying as an expert witness for the Camden 28, who were charged with breaking into one of these places.
swap.text: Name these places. Catholic priests Daniel and Phillip Berrigan were arrested for pouring homemade napalm over documents taken from one of these places in Catonsville, Maryland.
swap.answerHtml: draft boards [or draft offices; or selective service offices; accept equivalents that mention the draft or selective service]
